claim: A Direct Connect gateway only routes traffic from Direct Connect VIFs to virtual private gateways associated with VPCs, so traffic between two VPCs on the same Direct Connect gateway does not work; to send traffic between two VPCs you must configure a VPC peering connection.
question: Can traffic go from one VPC to another VPC through the same AWS Direct Connect gateway?

values.display: you must configure a VPC peering connection
values.spoken: a Direct Connect gateway does not route VPC to VPC; use VPC peering

qualifiers.condition: VPCs associated with the same Direct Connect gateway

evidence.quote: No, AWS Direct Connect gateway's only support routing traffic from AWS Direct Connect VIFs to VGW (associated with VPC). In order to send traffic between two VPCs, you must configure a VPC peering connection.

note: FAQ question: 'Can I send traffic from a VPC that is associated with an AWS Direct Connect gateway to another VPC associated to the same AWS Direct Connect gateway?' (item 139).

claim: An AWS Direct Connect gateway does not route traffic between a VPN and a Direct Connect VIF; to enable that, you create a VPN in the Region of the VIF and attach the VIF and the VPN to the same virtual private gateway.
question: Can a Direct Connect gateway route traffic between a VPN on a virtual private gateway and a Direct Connect VIF?

values.display: will not route traffic between a VPN and an AWS Direct Connect VIF
values.spoken: a Direct Connect gateway does not link a VPN to a VIF

qualifiers.condition: VPN attached to a virtual private gateway that is associated with the Direct Connect gateway

evidence.quote: No, an AWS Direct Connect gateway will not route traffic between a VPN and an AWS Direct Connect VIF. To enable this use case, you must create a VPN in the AWS Region of the VIF and attach the VIF and the VPN to the same VGW.

note: FAQ question: item 140 (VPN in us-east-1 attached to a VGW that is associated with a Direct Connect gateway).

claim: If a virtual private gateway has both a VPN and a Direct Connect gateway and the Direct Connect circuit goes down, VPC traffic routes out to the VPN as long as the VPC route table has routes to the virtual private gateway towards the VPN.
question: If a VGW is attached to a VPN and a Direct Connect gateway and the Direct Connect circuit goes down, does VPC traffic route out to the VPN?

values.display: as long as the VPC route table has routes to the virtual private gateway
values.spoken: traffic fails over to the VPN if the route table points to the virtual private gateway

qualifiers.condition: VPC route table has routes to the virtual private gateway towards the VPN

evidence.quote: Yes, as long as the VPC route table has routes to the virtual private gateway (VGW) towards the VPN.

claim: Private virtual interfaces and Direct Connect gateways must be in the same AWS account, and so must transit virtual interfaces and Direct Connect gateways; virtual private gateways and transit gateways can be in different accounts than the Direct Connect gateway owner.
question: Do private or transit VIFs, the Direct Connect gateway, the virtual private gateway and the transit gateway have to be in the same AWS account?

values.display: must be in the same AWS account
values.spoken: VIFs and their Direct Connect gateway share an account; gateways can be in other accounts

qualifiers.condition: private VIF and transit VIF with the Direct Connect gateway: same account; virtual private gateway and transit gateway: can be in different accounts

evidence.quote: Private virtual interfaces and AWS Direct Connect gateways must be in the same AWS account. Similarly, transit virtual interfaces and AWS Direct Connect gateways must be in the same AWS account. Virtual private gateway(s) and AWS Transit Gateway(s) can be in different AWS accounts than the account that owns the AWS Direct Connect gateway.

claim: There are no charges for using an AWS Direct Connect gateway; you pay applicable egress data charges based on the source remote Region, and port-hour charges.
question: Are there additional fees when using a Direct Connect gateway with remote AWS Regions?

values.display: no charges for using an AWS Direct Connect gateway
values.spoken: the Direct Connect gateway itself is free

qualifiers.condition: egress data charges and port-hour charges still apply

evidence.quote: There are no charges for using an AWS Direct Connect gateway. You will pay applicable egress data charges based on the source remote AWS Region and port hour charges.

claim: With a Direct Connect gateway, traffic takes the shortest path between your Direct Connect location and the destination AWS Region, regardless of the home Region of the location; it does not go through the home Region.
question: With a Direct Connect gateway, does traffic to the destination Region go through the associated home Region?

values.display: your traffic will take the shortest path
values.spoken: traffic takes the shortest path, not via the home Region

evidence.quote: When using AWS Direct Connect gateway, your traffic will take the shortest path to and from your AWS Direct Connect location to the destination AWS Region, regardless of the associated home AWS Region of the AWS Direct Connect location where you are connected.

claim: A VGW-VPC pair cannot be part of more than one AWS Direct Connect gateway.
question: Can a virtual private gateway associated with a VPC be part of more than one Direct Connect gateway?

values.display: cannot be part of more than one AWS Direct Connect gateway
values.spoken: a VGW-VPC pair belongs to one Direct Connect gateway

evidence.quote: No, a VGW-VPC pair cannot be part of more than one AWS Direct Connect gateway.

claim: One private virtual interface can only attach to one AWS Direct Connect gateway or one virtual private gateway.
question: Can you attach a private virtual interface to more than one Direct Connect gateway?

values.display: only attach to one AWS Direct Connect gateway OR one Virtual Private Gateway
values.spoken: a private VIF attaches to one gateway only

evidence.quote: No, one private virtual interface can only attach to one AWS Direct Connect gateway OR one Virtual Private Gateway.

claim: You cannot associate a virtual private gateway that is not attached to a VPC with an AWS Direct Connect gateway.
question: Can you attach a virtual private gateway to a Direct Connect gateway if it is not attached to a VPC?

values.display: you cannot associate an unattached VGW
values.spoken: the virtual private gateway must be attached to a VPC first

evidence.quote: No, you cannot associate an unattached VGW to AWS Direct Connect gateway.

claim: AWS Direct Connect gateway does not support AWS VPN CloudHub functionality, but if a Site-to-Site VPN connection is on a virtual gateway associated with your Direct Connect gateway, you can use the VPN connection for failover.
question: Does a Direct Connect gateway support VPN CloudHub, and can a VPN still serve as failover?

values.display: does not support AWS VPN CloudHub functionality
values.spoken: no CloudHub through a Direct Connect gateway, but a VPN can be the failover

qualifiers.condition: VPN connection to a virtual gateway associated with the Direct Connect gateway can be used for failover

evidence.quote: AWS Direct Connect gateway does not support AWS VPN CloudHub functionality. However, if you are using an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to a virtual gateway (VGW) that is associated with your AWS Direct Connect gateway, you can use your VPN connection for failover.

note: FAQ question: 'If I associate virtual private gateways (VGWs) to an AWS Direct Connect gateway, can I continue to use all VPC features?' (item 125). Item 131 says existing CloudHub works when a VIF is attached to a VGW directly; do not read this fact as 'CloudHub is gone'.

claim: Multi-account support lets you associate up to 20 VPCs or up to six AWS Transit Gateways from multiple AWS accounts with an AWS Direct Connect gateway.
question: What is multi-account support for the Direct Connect gateway and how many VPCs or transit gateways can it associate?

values.display: up to 20 Amazon Virtual Private Clouds
up to six AWS Transit Gateways

qualifiers.condition: associations come from multiple AWS accounts

evidence.quote: Multi-account support for AWS Direct Connect gateway is a feature that allows you to associate up to 20 Amazon Virtual Private Clouds (Amazon VPCs) or up to six AWS Transit Gateways from multiple AWS accounts with an AWS Direct Connect gateway.

note: FAQ question: 'What is multi-account support for AWS Direct Connect gateway?' (item 18).

claim: To use Direct Connect to transfer objects from a CloudFront origin in your own data center, you must have a Direct Connect public VIF, and if you filter route imports you must import all Anycast routes.
question: What do you need to use Direct Connect for a CloudFront origin in your own data center?

values.display: You must have a Direct Connect Public VIF
values.spoken: a public virtual interface is required for a CloudFront origin

qualifiers.condition: origin in your own data center; route imports filtered

evidence.quote: You must have a Direct Connect Public VIF and if you are filtering your route imports, you must ensure you import all Anycast routes.

note: FAQ question: 'If I’m using Amazon CloudFront and my origin is in my own data center, can I use AWS Direct Connect to transfer the objects stored in my own data center?' (item 52).

claim: Each Direct Connect connection can be configured with one or more virtual interfaces, so one connection can reach AWS services over public IP space and VPC resources over private IP space at the same time.
question: Can you use the same Direct Connect connection with a VPC and other AWS services simultaneously?

values.spoken: one connection can carry several virtual interfaces

evidence.quote: Each AWS Direct Connect connection can be configured with one or more virtual interfaces. Virtual interfaces may be configured to access AWS services such as Amazon EC2 and Amazon S3 using public IP space, or resources in a VPC using private IP space.

claim: If you do not specify Local Preference communities for your private VIF, the default local preference is based on the distance to the Direct Connect locations from the local Region, and egress behavior across multiple VIFs from multiple locations may be arbitrary.
question: What is the default behavior if you do not use the supported local preference communities on a private VIF?

values.display: the default local preference is based on the distance
values.spoken: without communities, preference follows distance and may be arbitrary across locations

evidence.quote: If you do not specify Local Preference communities for your private VIF, the default local preference is based on the distance to the AWS Direct Connect Locations from the local Region. In such situation, egress behavior across multiple VIFs from multiple AWS Direct Connect Locations may be arbitrary.

claim: You can build failover with local preference communities by advertising prefixes over the primary or active virtual interface with a community for higher local preference than the prefixes advertised over the backup or passive virtual interface.
question: Does the local preference communities feature support failover?

values.display: advertising prefixes over the primary/active virtual interface
values.spoken: give the primary VIF a higher local preference community than the backup

evidence.quote: This can be accomplished by advertising prefixes over the primary/active virtual interface with a community for higher local preference than prefixes advertised over the backup/passive virtual interface.

note: FAQ question: 'Does the local preference communities feature support failover?' (item 150).

claim: AWS provides an ASN of 64512 for the AWS Direct Connect gateway if you do not choose one.
question: Which ASN does AWS assign to a Direct Connect gateway if you do not provide one?

qualifiers.condition: no private ASN chosen at creation

evidence.quote: AWS will provide an ASN of 64512 for the AWS Direct Connect gateway if you don’t choose one.

claim: You cannot modify the AWS side ASN of a Direct Connect gateway after creation; you delete the gateway and recreate it with the desired private ASN.
question: Can you change the AWS side ASN after the Direct Connect gateway is created?

values.display: you cannot modify the AWS side ASN after creation
values.spoken: the AWS side ASN is fixed at creation

evidence.quote: No, you cannot modify the AWS side ASN after creation. You can delete the AWS Direct Connect gateway and recreate a new AWS Direct Connect gateway with the desired private ASN.

claim: For scheduled Direct Connect maintenance AWS sends 3 notifications, at 14 calendar days, 7 calendar days and 1 calendar day; emergency maintenance may happen at any time with up to 60-minute notification.
question: When are you informed about maintenance events on Direct Connect?

values.display: 14 calendar days, followed by 7 calendar days and followed by 1 calendar day

qualifiers.condition: emergency maintenance may be performed at any time with up to 60-minute notification depending on the maintenance

evidence.quote: Scheduled maintenance is planned and we provide 3 notifications - 14 calendar days, followed by 7 calendar days and followed by 1 calendar day notifications. Emergency maintenance may be performed at any time and you may receive up to 60-minute notification(s) depending upon the nature of the maintenance.
